name: Network partition: two primaries (split brain)
description: Each of two regions has its own API; DNS splits users evenly between them. The database's primary is in the east and its replica in the west, with automatic failover. The scenario cuts the network between the regions at 20 s for 40 s. The west cannot reach the primary and thinks it is down: after the failover time, the west replica becomes the new primary. But the old primary still runs, and east users still write to it: both sides take writes, and the data diverges when the partition ends (see the database's "Divergent writes" and the timeline). Try this: turn on the database's "Fence the old primary" and run again. No more divergence; the cost is that east writes fail during the partition.
